proposals.before: An edict dismissed Li from office. Shilun was made Jingyang Army military commissioner and acting metropolitan commissioner, and soon became prefect of Yan'an and concurrent commander of all Fuyan Circuit troops and horses.
proposals.after: An edict dismissed Li from office. Shilun was made Jiangyang Army military commissioner and acting metropolitan commissioner, and soon became prefect of Yan'an and concurrent commander of all Fuyan Circuit troops and horses.
proposals.reason: 絳陽 is Jiangyang, not Jingyang; 絳 is a distinct graph from 京 or 涇.

proposals.before: An edict dismissed Li from office; Shilun was transferred to Jingyang Army Military Commissioner, acting Metropolitan Commissioner, and soon became prefect of Yan'an and concurrent commander of all troops and horses of Fuyan Circuit.
proposals.after: An edict dismissed Li from office; Shilun was transferred to Jiangyang Army Military Commissioner, acting Metropolitan Commissioner, and soon became prefect of Yan'an and concurrent commander of all troops and horses of Fuyan Circuit.
proposals.reason: The source army name is 絳陽軍; Jingyang misreads 絳 as 京/涇.

proposals.before: Even so, I have already dispatched Ti Control Shizhan Wulixin and others to lead troops there.
proposals.after: Even so, I have already dispatched Controller Shizhan Wulixin and others to lead troops there.
proposals.reason: 提控 is the office Controller, not the unintelligible calque 'Ti Control'.

proposals.before: I regard Taiyuan as a vital strongpoint that must be contested and have dispatched Ti Control Shizhan Wulixin to lead regular troops and righteous-army militia together to plan recovery.
proposals.after: I regard Taiyuan as a vital strongpoint that must be contested and have dispatched Controller Shizhan Wulixin to lead regular troops and righteous-army militia together to plan recovery.
proposals.reason: The same 提控 office is again rendered as 'Ti Control' instead of Controller.

proposals.before: In the sixth month Baode Zhenwu Army commander Wang Zhang and crossbow-army commander Qi Zhen murdered their prefect Boshulu Yinshuge and wiped out his family, then forced officials, troops, and civilians to sign a joint report to the Lan headquarters accusing Yinshuge of tyranny, secretly forging arms, and plotting rebellion.
proposals.after: In the sixth month Baode Zhenwei Army commander Wang Zhang and crossbow-army commander Qi Zhen murdered their prefect Boshulu Yinshuge and wiped out his family, then forced officials, troops, and civilians to sign a joint report to the Lan headquarters accusing Yinshuge of tyranny, secretly forging arms, and plotting rebellion.
proposals.reason: 振威 is Zhenwei, not Zhenwu; the idiomatic rendering invents the wrong army name.

proposals.before: Shilun sent Guishun Army controller Gao Gui of Lan Prefecture to scout; Gui fled to the Great Yuan army with tallies of the city's troops, horses, and grain and told them how strong or weak the defenses were.
proposals.after: Shilun sent Guishun Army controller Gao Gui of Lan Prefecture to scout; Gui fled to the Great Yuan army with the numbers of the city's troops, horses, and grain and told them how strong or weak the defenses were.
proposals.reason: 數目 means numerical counts of men, horses, and grain, not credential tallies (牌/符).

proposals.before: The advocates of the plan replied that Hezhong lay north of the river, lacked palace buildings, and could not rival Bianliang, and the proposal died.
proposals.after: Those leading the discussion held that Hezhong lay north of the river, lacked palace buildings, and could not rival Bianliang, and the proposal died.
proposals.reason: 主議者 are the officials who rejected Hezhong, not advocates of the move; the idiomatic English reverses the stance.

proposals.before: A few li downstream warships barred their path. Enemy vessels fired "Heaven-Shaking Thunder" incendiary bombs in succession; in the flashes Board Eke saw few men aboard, hacked through the blockade, reached Tong Pass, and escaped into Wenxiang.
proposals.after: A few li downstream warships barred their path. The fleeing ships carried fire-projectors called "Heaven-Shaking Thunder" and fired them in succession; when the flashes lit up, they saw few northern troops on the blocking boats, hacked through the blockade, reached Tong Pass, and escaped into Wenxiang.
proposals.reason: Chinese 船中有齎火砲 belongs to the defeated fleet, and 見北船軍無幾人 is what the light revealed on the northern boats, not enemy ships firing the bombs.

proposals.before: Knowledgeable men said Hezhong had held out until strength was spent, not through cowardice in battle, and that Eke's punishment was unjust.
proposals.after: Knowledgeable men said Hezhong's defense was not wanting; it fell only when strength was exhausted, not from guilt in battle, and that therefore some considered Eke's death unjust.
proposals.reason: The version omits 城守不下 and 訛可之死 and turns 非戰之罪 into 'cowardice'.

proposals.before: On the night of gengyin in the twelfth month of the second year of Yuanguang, Emperor Xuanzong fell gravely ill. Prince Jing Shouchun entered first to attend him; Emperor Aizong arrived later and found the Donghua Gate already closed. Hearing that Prince Ying was inside, Aizong sent Bureau of Military Affairs officials and Eastern Palace Imperial Guard commander Yila Pu'a with troops to the Donghua Gate. Metropolitan inspector and imperial son-in-law Tudan Hezhu memorialized the empress dowager, received permission, took the tally-keys, and opened the gate.
proposals.after: On the night of gengyin in the twelfth month of the second year of Yuanguang, Emperor Xuanzong fell gravely ill. Prince Ying Shouchun entered first to attend him; Emperor Aizong arrived later and found the Donghua Gate already closed. Hearing that Prince Ying was inside, Aizong sent Bureau of Military Affairs officials and Eastern Palace Imperial Guard commander Yila Pu'a with troops to the Donghua Gate. Metropolitan inspector and imperial son-in-law Tudan Hezhu memorialized the empress (zhonggong), received permission, took the tally-keys, and opened the gate.
proposals.reason: 英王 is Prince Ying, not Jing; using both Prince Jing and Prince Ying in one sentence splits one man. 中宮 at Xuanzong's sickbed is the empress, not necessarily an empress dowager.

proposals.before: Emperor Xuanzong had renamed Henan Prefecture Jinchang Prefecture and styled it Central Capital, planned an imperial camp on Mount Shaoshi's summit, and ordered Yila Nihehe to build it; Henian was now posted as defender.
proposals.after: Emperor Xuanzong had renamed Henan Prefecture Jinchang Prefecture and styled it Central Capital, planned an imperial camp on Mount Shaoshi's summit, and ordered Yila Nianhe to build it; Henian was now posted as defender.
proposals.reason: Chinese 移剌粘合 corresponds to Yila Nianhe; English Nihehe is a corrupted transcription of 粘合.

proposals.before: Earlier Emperor Xuanzong changed Henan Prefecture to Jinchang Prefecture, styled Central Capital, and also planned the summit of Mount Shaoshi as an imperial camp, ordering Yila Nihehe to build it; at this time Sa Henian was defender.
proposals.after: Earlier Emperor Xuanzong changed Henan Prefecture to Jinchang Prefecture, styled Central Capital, and also planned the summit of Mount Shaoshi as an imperial camp, ordering Yila Nianhe to build it; at this time Sa Henian was defender.
proposals.reason: Chinese 移剌粘合 corresponds to Yila Nianhe; English Nihehe is a corrupted transcription of 粘合.

proposals.before: On jiashen of the third month more than a hundred Zhongxiao Army horsemen entered the envoy's residence, forcibly escorted Henian out to flee; Henian had no choice but to follow, taking officials and his son with him; they had just exited the south inner city gate when troops on the wall noticed, closed them in the barbican, arrows and stones rained down, and many men and horses were killed or wounded.
proposals.after: On jiashen of the third month more than a hundred Zhongxiao Army horsemen entered the official residence, forcibly escorted Henian out to flee; Henian had no choice but to follow, taking officials and his son with him; they had just exited the south inner city gate when troops on the wall noticed, closed them in the barbican, arrows and stones rained down, and many men and horses were killed or wounded.
proposals.reason: 使宅 is the defender's official residence, not an envoy's residence.

proposals.before: On bingchen of the fourth month the emperor summoned Minister Wentihen Shousun, censor-in-chief Wugusun Buji, libationer Peiman Ahudai, academician Pucha Shida, remonstrance officer Chen Gui, investigators Wugulun Sihe and Wanyan Xixian, and associate administrator of the Office of Imperial Kin Sa Henian to discuss the western front. The emperor said: "I have already ordered Heda to stake everything on one decisive battle."
proposals.after: On bingchen of the fourth month the emperor summoned Minister Wentihen Shousun, censor-in-chief Wugusun Buji, libationer Peiman Ahudai, academician Pucha Shida, right remonstrance officer Chen Gui, investigators Wugulun Sihe and Wanyan Xixian, and associate administrator of the Office of Imperial Kin Sa Henian to discuss the western front. The emperor said: "I have already ordered Heda to stake everything on one decisive battle."
proposals.reason: Chinese 右司諫 is specifically Right Remonstrance Officer; the idiomatic line drops 右, unlike the literal field.

proposals.before: Qiang Shen came from the grain-shooting army of Hedong; he was homely in appearance but possessed extraordinary strength.
proposals.after: Qiang Shen came from the grain-shooting army of Hezhong; he was homely in appearance but possessed extraordinary strength.
proposals.reason: Chinese 河中 is Hezhong, not Hedong (河東).

proposals.before: Early in the Xingding era he followed Hua deputy commander An Ning in retaking Tong Pass, was rewarded with appointment, and once supervised the Heyang vinegar monopoly.
proposals.after: Early in the Xingding era he followed Hua Prefecture Deputy Metropolitan Commander An Ning in retaking Tong Pass, was rewarded with appointment, and once supervised the Heyang vinegar monopoly.
proposals.reason: 華州副都統 is the Hua Prefecture deputy metropolitan commander; idiomatic English drops the prefecture and flattens 都統.

proposals.before: Central Capital had already fallen; defender Sa Henian had died; marshal Ren Shouzhen re-established headquarters and appointed Shen patrol commissioner on discretionary authority.
proposals.after: Central Capital had already fallen; defender and concurrent touring Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner, imperial clansman Sa Henian, had died in it; marshal Ren Shouzhen re-established headquarters and appointed Shen patrol commissioner on discretionary authority.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 兼行樞密院使, 內族, and 死之 (died in the fall).

proposals.before: Hutu was then Defender Who Breaks the Barbarians, stationed at Tong Pass. Ordered south the previous twelfth month, he reached Yanshi, heard of the crossing at Baipo, turned straight for Shaoshi, and reached Shaolin Temple that night.
proposals.after: Hutu was then Defender Who Breaks the Barbarians, stationed at Tong Pass. In the twelfth month of the previous winter he received orders to come in relief; he reached Yanshi, heard of the crossing at Baipo, turned straight for Shaoshi, and reached Shaolin Temple that night.
proposals.reason: Chinese 被旨入援 is an order to enter in relief, not a southward posting; 去冬十二月 is the previous winters twelfth month.

proposals.before: In the twelfth month Silie, who had kept his branch secretariat on the mountain at Central Capital, called up troops to hold Luoyang jointly, yet again delayed and would not march.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month Silie, from the mountain, placed his branch secretariat at Central Capital and called up troops to hold Luoyang jointly; Hutu again delayed and would not march.
proposals.reason: The delay 又遷延不行 continues Hutus earlier refusal; the next sentence is Silies ultimatum against that lingering, so the silent subject is Hutu not Silie.

proposals.before: In the sixth month the enemy pressed harder. Qiang Shen was fighting with all his strength, but Hutu at once led light cavalry away with his wife and children, abandoned the south of the city, and fled, and Central Capital was lost.
proposals.after: In the sixth month the enemy pressed harder. Qiang Shen was fighting with all his strength, but Hutu at once led light cavalry away with his wife and children, abandoned the city, and fled south, and Central Capital was lost.
proposals.reason: Abandoned-the-city-and-fled-south is the sense of 棄城南奔, not abandoned the south of the city.

proposals.before: Earlier when Hutu was dismissed from machine government he had many complaints; attendants urged the emperor to put him to death, but the emperor would not listen.
proposals.after: Earlier when Hutu was dismissed from confidential government affairs he had many complaints; attendants urged the emperor to put him to death, but the emperor would not listen.
proposals.reason: 機政 is confidential or central government business, not a machine government.

proposals.before: Soon commander-in-chief Shulutu Loushi and Hutu were both made acting participating administrators. Loushi worked with right chancellor Zhongde while Hutu continued his defense. Defender Chenglins was again made eastern marshal with acting overall command.
proposals.after: Soon commander-in-chief Bozhulu Loushi and Hutu were both made acting participating administrators. Loushi worked with right chancellor Zhongde while Hutu continued his defense. Defender Chenglin was again made eastern marshal with acting overall command.
proposals.reason: 孛術魯 is the Jurchen surname Bozhulu, not Shulutu; 承麟 is Chenglin, not Chenglins.

proposals.before: On the second day the attack shifted to the south wall and Wugulun Hao took over. Catapults nearly brought down the tower. Right chancellor Zhongde led a relief force and the assault was called off.
proposals.after: On the second day the attack shifted to the south wall. Wugulun Hao made light of it; catapults nearly brought down the tower. Right chancellor Zhongde led a relief force and the assault was called off.
proposals.reason: 易之 means Hao treated the south-wall attack as easy, not that he replaced the previous commander.

proposals.before: Silie of the inner clan was the son of Prince of Nanyang, Wang Xiang.
proposals.after: Silie of the inner clan was the son of Xiang, Prince of Nanyang.
proposals.reason: 襄 is the personal name of the Prince of Nanyang; 王 here is the noble title 郡王, not the Chinese surname Wang.

proposals.before: Of the inner clan, Silie was son of Prince Nanyang Wang Xiang.
proposals.after: Of the inner clan, Silie was son of Xiang, Prince of Nanyang.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 南陽郡王襄 as a surname-plus-given-name Wang Xiang.

proposals.before: In the first year of Tianxing Bian was besieged. The Aizong made Silie acting participating administrator and sent him to direct branch secretariat affairs at Dengzhou.
proposals.after: In the first year of Tianxing, Bian was besieged. The Aizong made Silie acting participating administrator and sent him to direct branch secretariat affairs at Dengzhou.
proposals.reason: Tianxing is the era name and Bian the capital; the English fuses them into one proper noun.

proposals.before: He was bright and sharp, unrestrained by convention, broadly learned and skilled in discussion, adept at documents, and wrote with a clear, beautiful hand in the manner of the Jin period.
proposals.after: He was bright and sharp, unrestrained by convention, broadly learned and skilled in discussion, adept at documents, and wrote with a clear, beautiful hand in the manner of the Jin-dynasty (晉) masters.
proposals.reason: 晉人風 refers to Western Jin calligraphy, not the Jin 金 dynasty of this history.

proposals.before: Bright and sharp, unrestrained by convention, broadly learned and skilled at discussion, adept at documents, writing clear and beautiful with Jin-ren style.
proposals.after: Bright and sharp, unrestrained by convention, broadly learned and skilled at discussion, adept at documents, writing clear and beautiful in the style of the Jin (晉) masters.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise treats 晉人 as if it were the Jin 金 house.

proposals.before: In the twelfth month he acted as commander-in-chief of the Shandong West and East circuits, and also held the posts of military commissioner of the Military Pacification Army and observation commissioner within Xuzhou.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month he conducted the affairs of the commander-in-chief of the Shandong West Circuit, and also held the posts of military commissioner of the Wuning Army and observation commissioner within Xuzhou.
proposals.reason: 山東西路 is the West Shandong circuit, not two circuits; 武甯軍 is the Wuning Army.

proposals.before: Several hundred Song horsemen came out to resist. Yawuta feigned a northward retreat, sprang an ambush, and beheaded two hundred men.
proposals.after: Several hundred Song horsemen came out to resist. Yawuta feigned defeat, sprang an ambush, and beheaded two hundred men.
proposals.reason: 佯北 means a feigned rout/defeat (北 as ‘to be beaten’), not a retreat northward.

proposals.before: Song men came out with several hundred horsemen to resist; Yawuta commanded troops to feign retreat north, sprang ambush and struck them, beheading two hundred.
proposals.after: Song men came out with several hundred horsemen to resist; Yawuta commanded troops to feign defeat, sprang an ambush and struck them, beheading two hundred.
proposals.reason: 佯北 is feigned defeat, not ‘retreat north’.

proposals.before: Shi Qing stood on the wall directing the defense. A shot struck Yawuta in the eye, and Shi Qing then withdrew his force south in flight.
proposals.after: Shi Qing stood on the wall directing the defense. A shot struck him in the eye, and he then withdrew his force south in flight.
proposals.reason: 射中其目 follows 時青乘城指麾; 其 refers to Shi Qing, who then fled, not to Yawuta.

proposals.before: Shi Qing stood on the wall commanding; a shot struck Yawuta in the eye, whereupon Shi Qing withdrew his force south in flight.
proposals.after: Shi Qing stood on the wall commanding; a shot struck his eye, whereupon he withdrew his force south in flight.
proposals.reason: 其目 is Shi Qing’s eye; the English inserts Yawuta against the Chinese referent.

proposals.before: After Liuge was killed the people still resisted. As Yawuta was pressing the assault, Song chief Liu Bin, superintendent Huang Wen, and others sent the heads of the rebels Luan Yanjun, Qi Yi, and Wanyan Qige, and displayed the head of superintendent Jinshan Bada, dispatching their adjutants Ma Jun and Wu Gui to present them.
proposals.after: After Liuge was killed the people still resisted. As Yawuta was pressing the assault, Song chief Liu Bin, superintendent Huang Wen, and others bound the ringleaders Yan Jun, Qi Yi, and Wanyan Qige, and displayed the head of superintendent Jinshan Bada, dispatching their adjutants Ma Jun and Wu Gui to present them.
proposals.reason: 顏俊 is Yan Jun, not Luan Yanjun; 縛首亂 means they bound the ringleaders (whose heads were then offered).

proposals.before: After Liuge was killed the masses still resisted; as he was pressing the assault, Song chief Liu Bin, superintendent Huang Wen, and others bound the heads of the rebels Luan Yanjun, Qi Yi, Wanyan Qige, and displayed the head of superintendent Jinshan Bada, sending their adjutants Ma Jun and Wu Gui to present them.
proposals.after: After Liuge was killed the masses still resisted; as he was pressing the assault, Song chief Liu Bin, superintendent Huang Wen, and others bound the ringleader rebels Yan Jun, Qi Yi, and Wanyan Qige, and displayed the head of superintendent Jinshan Bada, sending their adjutants Ma Jun and Wu Gui to present them.
proposals.reason: 顏俊 is Yan Jun; 首亂 is ringleader, not a surname Luan.

proposals.before: Prince Jing Shouchun said, "For all who serve as generals and commanders, controlling talent should all be like this."
proposals.after: Prince Ying Shouchun said, "For all who serve as generals and commanders, controlling talent should all be like this."
proposals.reason: 英王 is Prince Ying, not Prince Jing.

proposals.before: Prince Jing Shouchun said: "For all who serve as generals and commanders, controlling talent should all be like this."
proposals.after: Prince Ying Shouchun said: "For all who serve as generals and commanders, controlling talent should all be like this."
proposals.reason: 英王 is Prince Ying, not Prince Jing.

proposals.before: That year, after Great Yuan forces had destroyed the Xia state, they attacked Dexun, Qinzhou, Qingshui, and other cities in Shaanxi, then entered Jingzhao from Fengxiang. Guanzhong was shaken to its core.
proposals.after: That year, after Great Yuan forces had destroyed the Xia state, they attacked Deshun, Qinzhou, Qingshui, and other cities in Shaanxi, then entered Jingzhao from Fengxiang. Guanzhong was shaken to its core.
proposals.reason: Chinese 德順 is the prefecture Deshun, not Dexun.

proposals.before: That year, after Great Yuan forces had destroyed Xia, they attacked Dexun, Qinzhou, Qingshui, and other cities in Shaanxi, then entered Jingzhao from Fengxiang; Guanzhong shook greatly.
proposals.after: That year, after Great Yuan forces had destroyed Xia, they attacked Deshun, Qinzhou, Qingshui, and other cities in Shaanxi, then entered Jingzhao from Fengxiang; Guanzhong shook greatly.
proposals.reason: Chinese 德順 is Deshun; Dexun is a mistranscription.

proposals.before: In the twelfth month an edict appointed Yawuta and Vice Censor-in-Chief Pu'a to hold acting signatures at the Bureau of Military Affairs, while imperial clansman Wanyan Eke was to lead troops to relieve Qingyang.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month an edict appointed Yawuta and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Pu'a to hold acting signatures at the Bureau of Military Affairs, while imperial clansman Wanyan Eke was to lead troops to relieve Qingyang.
proposals.reason: 副樞 is vice-commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, not Vice Censor-in-Chief.

proposals.before: In the twelfth month an edict appointed Yawuta with Vice Censor-in-Chief Pu'a to hold acting signatures at the Bureau of Military Affairs; imperial clansman Eke was to lead troops to relieve Qingyang.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month an edict appointed Yawuta with Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Pu'a to hold acting signatures at the Bureau of Military Affairs; imperial clansman Eke was to lead troops to relieve Qingyang.
proposals.reason: 副樞 names the military bureau vice-commissioner, not a censorate office.

proposals.before: He qualified as jinshi in the first year of Zhiyou.
proposals.after: He qualified as jinshi in the first year of Zhining.
proposals.reason: 至甯 is 至寧 (Zhining, AD 1213), not Zhiyou.

proposals.before: He gained his jinshi degree in the first year of Zhiyou.
proposals.after: He gained his jinshi degree in the first year of Zhining.
proposals.reason: 至甯元年 is Zhining 1, not a Zhiyou era.

proposals.before: He was transferred to right secretariat director, Henan South Circuit director of agriculture, and became Hezhong circuit administrator.
proposals.after: He was transferred to Director of the Right Office, Jingnan Circuit assistant director of agriculture, and became Hezhong Circuit administrator.
proposals.reason: 京南路 is Jingnan Circuit, not Henan South; 右司都事 is Director of the Right Office.

proposals.before: He was transferred to Right Secretariat Director, Henan South Circuit Director of Agriculture, and became Hezhong Circuit Administrator.
proposals.after: He was transferred to Director of the Right Office, Jingnan Circuit Director of Agriculture, and became Hezhong Circuit Administrator.
proposals.reason: 京南路 is Jingnan Circuit; Henan South is a mistranslation.

decisions.reason: 絳陽軍 is Jiangyang Army; Jingyang would require 京 or 涇, not 絳.
The literal field likewise misreads 絳陽軍 as Jingyang; Jiangyang matches 絳.
提控 is the office controller; the calque Ti Control is not English and is not a name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 臣已遣提控石盞吾里忻等領軍以往矣

decisions.reason: The same 提控 office is again written as Ti Control; Controller is the correct rendering.

decisions.reason: 振威軍 is Zhenwei Army; Zhenwu would be 振武, a different name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 保德州振威軍萬戶王章

decisions.reason: The original compresses 德順 into Hezhong and turns 非戰之罪 into cowardice; the proposal restores 城守不下 and 訛可之死 but still omits 德順 as a place.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 識者以為河中城守不下，德順力竭而陷，非戰之罪，故訛可之死，人有冤之者

decisions.reason: 英王 is Prince Ying, not Jing, and 中宮 at the dying emperor's bedside is the empress, not an empress dowager.

decisions.reason: 移剌粘合 transcribes as Yila Nianhe; Nihehe corrupts 粘合.

使宅 is the defender's official residence, not an envoy's lodging.

河中 is Hezhong; Hedong would be 河東.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 從華州副都統安寧複潼關

decisions.reason: The original omits 兼行樞密院使, 內族, and 死之 (died in the fall).

sourceWitness.excerpt: 留守兼行樞密院使內族撒合輦死之

decisions.reason: 被旨入援 is an order to come in relief, not a southward posting; 去冬十二月 is the previous winter's twelfth month.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以去冬十二月被旨入援

decisions.reason: 又遷延不行 continues Hutu's earlier lingering; Silie's next 檄 threatens that delay, so the silent subject is Hutu, not Silie.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 徵兵同保洛陽，又遷延不行

decisions.reason: 棄城南奔 is abandon the city and flee south, not abandon the south of the city.
機政 is confidential or pivotal government business; machine government is a false calque of 機.
孛術魯 is the surname Bozhulu, not Shulutu; 承麟 is Chenglin, not Chenglins.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 總帥孛術魯婁室……都尉承麟

decisions.reason: 易之 means Hao made light of the south-wall attack; it does not mean he took over command.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 二日移攻南城，烏古論鎬易之

decisions.reason: 襄 is the personal name of the Prince of Nanyang; 王 is the title 郡王, not the surname Wang.
The literal field makes the same Wang Xiang error for 南陽郡王襄.
In the first year of Tianxing Bian was besieged already names the era and the capital as separate words; adding a comma is only punctuation.

decisions.after: He was bright and sharp, unrestrained by convention, broadly learned and skilled in discussion, adept at documents, and wrote with a clear, beautiful hand in the manner of the Wei-Jin calligraphers.
decisions.reason: The original Jin period is ambiguous with the Jin house of this history; the proposal's parenthetical graph is not allowed in the English field. Wei-Jin names the calligraphic tradition meant by the source.

decisions.after: Bright and sharp, unrestrained by convention, broadly learned and skilled at discussion, adept at documents, writing clear and beautiful in the style of the Wei-Jin masters.
decisions.reason: Jin-ren style leaves the two Jin dynasties confused, and the proposed English still inserts a Chinese graph. Wei-Jin is the intended calligraphic manner.
山東西路 is the West Shandong circuit, not west and east circuits; 武甯軍 is the Wuning Army, not Military Pacification Army.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 行山東西路兵馬都總管府事，兼武甯軍節度使

decisions.reason: 佯北 is a feigned defeat (敗北), not a retreat northward.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 牙吾塔麾兵佯北，發伏擊之

decisions.reason: The literal feign retreat north makes the same 北-as-north error.
射中其目 follows 時青乘城指麾; 其 and the ensuing 南奔 refer to Shi Qing, not Yawuta.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時青乘城指麾，射中其目，遂拔眾南奔

decisions.reason: The literal field invents Yawuta as the patient of 其目 against the same Chinese referent.
顏俊 is Yan Jun; 縛首亂 means they bound the ringleaders, while only 梟……首 beheads Jinshan Bada. Luan Yanjun is a ghost name from 亂.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 縛首亂顏俊、戚誼、完顏乞哥，及梟提控金山八打首

decisions.reason: The literal bound the heads of the rebels Luan Yanjun repeats the 首亂/顏俊 misread; ringleader Yan Jun is correct.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 縛首亂顏俊、戚誼、完顏乞哥

decisions.reason: 英王守純 is Prince Ying Shouchun, not Prince Jing.
The literal field has the same Jing-for-英 error.
德順 is Deshun; Dexun is a mistranscription.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 進攻陝西德順、秦州、清水等城

decisions.reason: The literal field likewise writes Dexun for 德順.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 陝西德順、秦州、清水等城

decisions.reason: 副樞 is vice-commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, not Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 牙吾塔與副樞蒲阿權簽樞密院事

decisions.reason: The literal field repeats the censorate misreading of 副樞.
至甯元年 is Zhining 1 (至寧); Zhiyou is not this era name.
The literal field makes the same Zhiyou error for 至甯.
京南路 is Jingnan Circuit, not Henan South; 司農丞 is an assistant director of agriculture, not director.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 轉右司都事、京南路司農丞

decisions.after: He was transferred to Director of the Right Office, Jingnan Circuit Assistant Director of Agriculture, and became Hezhong Circuit Administrator.
decisions.reason: Jingnan correctly replaces Henan South, but the proposed literal still renders 司農丞 as Director of Agriculture; 丞 is the assistant post.

claimRetractions.reason: 縛首亂顏俊 records binding the ringleader Yan Jun; 梟首 is stated only for Jinshan Bada, so this death-by-head-presentation claim comes from the bad translation.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 縛首亂顏俊、戚誼、完顏乞哥，及梟提控金山八打首

claimRetractions.reason: 戚誼 is named among those bound as ringleaders, not among those whose heads were displayed.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 縛首亂顏俊、戚誼、完顏乞哥

claimRetractions.reason: 完顏乞哥 is likewise bound as a ringleader; the Chinese does not say he was killed and his head presented.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 縛首亂顏俊、戚誼、完顏乞哥

value.assessment: Hezhong fell from exhausted strength, not battle-guilt; some thought his death unjust
Hezhong's defense was not wanting and Deshun fell from exhausted strength, not from battle-guilt; some thought Eke's death unjust

claimRevisions.reason: The repaired sentence distinguishes Hezhong's defense from Deshun's fall by exhausted strength; the old assessment had collapsed both into Hezhong.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 河中城守不下，德順力竭而陷，非戰之罪，故訛可之死

claimRevisions.reason: 英王守純 is Prince Ying; Prince Jing exists only in the unrepaired English.
中宮 is the empress; empress dowager is not in the Chinese.
The English name Nihehe was produced by misreading 粘合; Nianhe is the matching transcription.
孛術魯婁室 is Bozhulu Loushi; Shulutu is a false English surname.
承麟 is Chenglin; the terminal s is not in the Chinese.
襄 is the given name; Wang was wrongly taken from the title 郡王.
顏俊 is Yan Jun; Luan Yanjun was invented by reading 亂 as a surname.
英王 is Prince Ying, not Prince Jing.
